name: ComMarker Omni XE UV
tagline: Expanded UV platform for larger glass and plastic work
tldr: Omni XE sits between Omni 1 and Omni X in ComMarker's UV lineup: check current specs for bed size and power. UV remains specialized: glass, plastics, fine detail.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

priceRange.note: Official ComMarker store, Oct 2026: $3,299 to $6,789 depending on 6W or 12W and bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

pros: Same UV source options, 10,000 mm/s galvo and LiDAR autofocus as the Omni X for $300 less
20 kg and 320 × 511 × 576 mm: easier to move and to fit on a bench than the enclosed Omni X
Open layout gives easier access for large or awkward objects and rotary setups
cons: Rated Class 4: 355 nm-rated safety glasses and a controlled room are mandatory
No door sensor or safety key, unlike the Omni X
ComMarker's 99.72% dust isolation claim applies to the enclosed Omni X: plan your own fume extraction

faq.question: Why is the Omni XE cheaper than the Omni X?
faq.answer: It drops the light-proof enclosure. ComMarker rates the XE as a Class 4 laser with a safety shield but no OD rating, door sensor or safety key, which brings the weight down to 20 kg (Omni X: 32 kg) and the price to $3,299 for the 6W basic bundle, $300 below the Omni X. Laser source, speed, autofocus and work areas are the same.

faq.question: What safety gear does the Omni XE need?
faq.answer: As a Class 4 UV laser, it needs 355 nm-rated safety glasses for everyone in the room, a space where nobody walks in unprotected during jobs, and fume extraction. ComMarker includes safety goggles in the bundles. If you cannot control the room, the enclosed Omni X is the safer purchase.

faq.question: 6W or 12W Omni XE?
faq.answer: The 12W basic bundle costs $5,699 against $3,299 for the 6W (ComMarker store, October 2026). It brings a 250 × 250 mm field instead of 150 × 150 mm and more multi-pass cutting capacity: 12 mm basswood, 10 mm acrylic and 1 mm stainless, against 8 mm, 6 mm and 0.6 mm for the 6W. For glass, crystal and fine marking, the 6W is usually enough.

standoutFeatures.title: Omni X performance for $300 less
standoutFeatures.body: Same 355 nm source options, 10,000 mm/s galvo, LiDAR autofocus and 3D internal engraving support as the Omni X, from $3,299 for the 6W basic bundle (October 2026).

standoutFeatures.title: Open frame for awkward objects
standoutFeatures.body: Without a full enclosure, tall bottles, tools and rotary setups are easier to position. ComMarker lists the same 235 mm maximum processing height as the Omni X, in a 20 kg machine.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 6W base version on ComMarker Omni XE UV. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Omni-XE UV targets heat-sensitive plastics and thin films: run vendor parameter cards on scrap. Do not assume Omni-X UV presets transfer without retesting.
primaryUse: Engraving-first desktop diode for makers who prioritize mark quality over cut speed

editorialDepth.advantages: ComMarker Omni XE UV targets glass, films, and heat-sensitive plastics: profitable when you already sell those jobs, not for casual UV experiments.
editorialDepth.limitations: Poor first-laser purchase. No wood or metal cutting. Confirm the module material list before buying the chassis.
